stigma extracts contain a substance which is released during stigma maturation and inhibits self-pollen protein synthesis.
the inhibition of germination by stigma extracts is dependent on the concentration and the time of addition of the extract and on protein synthesis in self-pollen.
stigma extracts contain a water-soluble substance that inhibits protein synthesis in self-pollen and that this inhibition is required for the expression of self-incompati-bility.

the biochemical basis of incompatibility.
the biochemical and physiological mechanisms of pollen protein synthesis and the role of pollen proteins in the regulation of pollen germination and incompatibility.
the biochemical basis of self-incompatiblity in Brassica.

self-incompatibility in Brassicaceae is controlled by the inhibition of protein synthesis in self pollen.
the inhibition of germination of self-pollen by stigmas of cabbage is due to a water-soluble inhibitor, which is produced in the stigmatic papillae and which is released when the stigmas are excised.
the inhibition is not due to the action of an inhibitor, but rather to the absence of an activator.

the stigma controls the expression of self-incompatibilty through the synthesis of a substance that is released into the medium.
self-incompatibility in Brassicacae is a form of gametophytic self-incompatibility.

the inhibition of germination by stigma extracts is not a simple reflection of the inhibition of protein synthesis but rather that the regulation of protein synthesis is the key to the control of germination.
the regulation of incompatibility is not a simple process.
